# Exact onboarding and design-charter verdict

**REVISE through six finite teaching/editorial corrections, NWX-01–06. Conditional acceptance of the six corrected manuscripts as authored teaching drafts is authorized once the named corrections and checks below are fulfilled. No additional generic source-authoring conference is required.**

Mira’s selected build, inventory totals and numerical two-turn sequence are correct. The required changes make omitted choices, recovery history and example prerequisites explicit, correct the stale crafting status, and distinguish the two meanings of “charter.”

**The completed crafting gate carries forward unchanged: 687/687 recipes and 433/433 public recipes remain reviewed.** This verdict promotes no pending class, spell or feat and does not close DD-01.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}[Complete exact verdict](sandbox:/mnt/data/onboarding_exact_reviewer/NWX_Onboarding_and_Charter_Exact_Verdict.md) · :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}[Verdict, exact correction register, audit and focused checks](sandbox:/mnt/data/DD_Onboarding_Charter_Exact_Reviewer_Verdict_and_Evidence.zip)

## What I inspected

The archive matches the supplied **2,985,983 bytes** and SHA-256:

`ef1e3c0c4d865de2295662fa94e13ba25f2be250ff918b3c133779445ded2302`

I opened the README, manifest, added scope and original case file, verified all **72 payload hashes**, and read **all six complete manuscripts**.

| Manuscript | Disposition |
|---|---|
| **FIRST_BARD_WALKTHROUGH** | Keep the build, selected effects, inventory and arithmetic; apply NWX-01, NWX-02 and NWX-04. |
| **SESSION_ZERO_PLAYTEST** | **KEEP** the complete six-step procedure and twelve-row agreement. No content correction required. |
| **NEWCOMER_PLAYER_GUIDE** | Apply NWX-01, NWX-02 and NWX-03. |
| **NEWCOMER_DIRECTOR_GUIDE** | Apply NWX-01, NWX-02 and NWX-05. |
| **RESONANCE_CHEATSHEET** | Apply NWX-02. |
| **DESIGN_CHARTER_CANDIDATE** | Keep the source-grounded editorial synthesis with NWX-06’s clarification. **DD-01 remains open.** |

I compared Mira against the actual selected Human, Nomadic Human, Battlefield Medic, Bard foundation, acquisition schedule, four Base cards, four ordinary spells and equipment records. I also checked the relevant Core, combat, conditions, healing, carrying, strain, spell-integration and Oracle engine provisions.

For the charter, I checked the locked doctrine, relevant gameplay-loop sections, supplied Player Rulebook introduction/advancement extract, character foundation, canon registry and existing expedition/Haven source-case boundaries. I did not undertake cosmology, deep-setting or seasonal interpretation.

The read-only audit produced **200 passing checks**: 75 integrity, 30 selected-source equality, 10 selected-source membership, 68 reference-arithmetic and 17 receipt-continuity checks. All **16 exact replacement locations** also matched uniquely in an in-memory editorial check. **No submitted file was modified.** These are not executed encounter-runtime tests or human teaching/balance evidence. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}[Audit record](sandbox:/mnt/data/onboarding_exact_reviewer/evidence/ONBOARDING_READ_ONLY_AUDIT.json)

The advanced promotion and navigation receipts were inspected for continuity, including hashes for fourteen included final artifacts. I am carrying forward the fulfilled authority, not claiming to have independently repeated its entire historical 138-input promotion audit.

## Mira: findings retained

### Creation, repertoire and equipment

The actual increases produce **STR 11, DEX 15, CON 15, INT 13, WIS 10, CHA 16**, with modifiers **0, +2, +2, +1, 0, +3**. Bard 1 correctly starts at **10 HP, PB +2 and 2 RP**.

Her seven distinct trained skills, DEX/CHA save proficiency, five tool proficiencies and Common/Dwarvish literacy match the selected records. The background relationships remain qualitative grants requiring actual campaign groups, not invented factions or numerical standing.

The four Base selections are eligible and separate from the two cantrips and two ranked spells. **S 1, C 3, attack +5, DC 13 and Limit 7 are correct.** NWX-04 clarifies that C is the printed-effect Charisma value, not Crescendo.

The inventory correctly totals **50.5 + 8.3 = 58.8 lb**, including coins, containers, full waterskin, five rations and the ten-charge healer’s kit. Backpack contents are **22.5 lb**; pouch contents are **0.3 lb**. At **5.88 Load**, Mira exceeds the **5.5 Burden threshold** while remaining within her **11 Load / 165 lb capacities**. **Speed 20** and the stated movement-check disadvantages follow.

The text correctly requires actual shape, volume, attachment and access checks. The weight calculation does not prove that everything physically fits. No tinderbox, extra instrument or free kit is added.

Leather **AC 13**, dagger **+4 / 1d4+2 piercing**, and thrown **20/60** remain correct. These findings are supported by the selected records preserved in `FIRST_BARD_WALKTHROUGH_PREPARATION.json` and the actual foundation, ancestry/background and equipment files identified in the full verdict.

### Two-turn sequence

After explicitly selecting **Mobile** under NWX-01, no existing numerical result changes:

| Checkpoint | Mira HP / RP | Crescendo / last performance | Enemy HP | Other state |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Initial | 10 / 2 | 0 / none | 30 | Dissonance 0; recharge ready |
| Verse hits for raw 4 | 10 / 2 | 1 / Verse | 26 | Ally’s encouragement recorded |
| Echo paid | 10 / 1 | 1 / Echo | 26 | Raw 4 stored; Echo recharge 2 |
| Mira takes 3 damage | 7 / 1 | 0 / none | 26 | No Wound trigger; pending Echo survives |
| Next regular start | 7 / 1 | 0 / none | 24 | Reaction refresh; Echo 2→1; copied damage 2 |
| Note paid; save fails | 7 / 0 | 1 / Note | 24 | Note recharge 2; target loses Reaction, not Action |

Dissonance remains zero. On the following regular start, Echo becomes ready and Note reaches 1, but readiness supplies neither RP nor another action. The scene does not establish an entire encounter’s outcome, a bestiary profile or balance.

The ordinary-spell sequence also correctly gives **0 / 0 / 1 / 0 / 2 Dissonance**. Retune’s calculated recovery is **4**, capped by Mira’s **2-RP maximum**. Bard 2 raises maximum HP to **17** and maximum RP to **3** without healing current HP, refilling current RP or restoring an already spent Hit Die. These are retained under the actual Bard, spell-integration and character-foundation procedures.

## Required corrections

The linked correction register contains **exact old/replacement blocks for all sixteen locations**. The following are the controlling changes; unchanged surrounding instructions remain in place.

### NWX-01 — Teach required stance selection and declare Mira’s stance

**Affected:** Player Guide, Director Guide and Mira §5.  
**Earlier rule: KEEP** `COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md`, **Stances**, submitted lines 113–123.

The turn summaries omit a required choice. Mira’s scene therefore leaves unspecified a state that could alter AC, movement or Reaction permission.

Add after the Player Guide’s turn-resource table:

> A stance is also a required regular-turn choice. Choose one during your regular turn before the first attack, spell, relevant check/save or movement that would use its benefit or restriction; if none occurs, choose before turn end. It lasts until your next regular-turn start. Selection is not retroactive, and an extra turn neither selects a new stance nor replenishes its spent allowance. Use the complete Aggressive, Guarded, Mobile, Focused or Carrying procedure in the combat guide; do not assume a neutral default. The choices can change AC, movement, damage or Reaction permission.

Append to the Director Guide’s regular-start paragraph:

> After mandatory start processing, prompt the player to choose one stance before the first event that would use its benefit or restriction, or before turn end if no such event occurs. Apply its actual AC, movement, damage and Reaction consequences; do not supply an unprinted neutral stance. Extra turns retain the existing stance and its spent allowances.

In Mira §5, **before the first Verse**, insert:

> Mira chooses Mobile before acting. For this example she makes no movement or opportunity attack, so Mobile changes none of the listed AC, Speed, attack or damage values. It grants no free movement.

Before the second turn’s Dissonant Note, **after the automatic start effects and Echo resolution**, insert:

> After the automatic start effects in step 4 resolve, Mira chooses Mobile again before acting. She again makes no movement or opportunity attack.

This supplies an existing choice, not a new neutral stance or permission to ignore Burden.

### NWX-02 — Distinguish Retune from the long-rest repetition reset

**Affected:** Resonance sheet **Recovery**; Player Guide **Rest and recovery**; Director Guide **Teach the current magic configuration**; Mira §8.  
**Earlier rule: KEEP** `SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md`, **Recovery bridge and unresolved integration**, lines 130–134, with the existing beneficial-rest limits.

The summaries correctly clear Dissonance but omit the different treatment of remembered spell identity and Refrain.

The corrected short-rest instruction is:

> Retune once: recover `max(0, round-half-up(maximum RP / 4) + primary RP class casting modifier)`, capped at maximum; clear Dissonance. Keep the remembered ordinary-spell name and Refrain counter unless an actual class feature expressly resets them.

The corrected long-rest instruction is:

> Restore RP to maximum, clear Dissonance, clear the remembered ordinary-spell name and reset its Refrain counter to 0.

Apply those distinctions consistently in the Player and Director paragraphs. Preserve the existing rest caps, interruption requirements and resource-specific recovery rules. A Rest Watch that only clears eligible Rest Debt does not become an additional beneficial long rest.

Append to Mira’s Retune example:

> Retune does not clear Mira’s remembered ordinary-spell name or Refrain counter. In the §7 sequence, a short rest after the fifth turn clears Dissonance but leaves Message and its second-repeat history; another legal Message would be the third repeat and add 3 Dissonance. A beneficial completed long rest instead clears the remembered name and resets that counter, so the next legal Message begins a new sequence.

No RP amount or original five-turn result changes.

### NWX-03 — Complete the generic healer-kit stabilization instruction

**Affected:** Player Guide, **Help someone at zero HP**, first sentence of its stabilization paragraph.  
**Earlier rules: KEEP** the Core stabilization procedure and `EQUIPMENT_ITEM_PROCEDURES.md`, introductory use rule and healer-kit row.

Replace the abbreviated sentence with:

> Use an Action and a DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check to stabilize a living dying creature under the Core procedure. Alternatively, an Action and one actual healer’s-kit charge automatically stabilize an adjacent living dying creature; this requires an available hand and access to the kit under the item procedures. Normal retrieval and hand-occupancy rules still apply. Stabilization alone restores no HP; an actual feature such as Trauma Response supplies only its own additional recovery.

Keep the remainder: Stable at zero HP, unconsciousness, the recorded 1d4-hour deadline, further damage, temporary-HP limits and no ordinary revival.

**Do not add a kit-charge requirement or a new proficiency gate to the alternative Medicine-check route.** Mira’s own emergency-aid example already contains the necessary physical and recovery predicates and is retained.

### NWX-04 — Complete the intervention examples’ starting states and define C

**Affected:** Mira §2 notation and §6 Chant/Shield examples.  
**Earlier rules: KEEP** the selected Bard cards and engine, ordinary-healing caps, focus/hand rules and the actual operational `shield` record.

Replace the notation sentence with:

> **Performance attack +5; performance DC 13; S = 1 song die and C = max(1, Charisma modifier) = 3.** C is the printed-effect Charisma value, not Mira’s changing Crescendo stack count.

Replace the **Healing with 2 RP** paragraph with:

> **Healing with 2 RP.** At her regular-turn start in this separate genuine encounter, Mira has 2 RP, 0 Crescendo, no last performance and no concentration. After mandatory start processing, she chooses Mobile before her first performance of the turn. She and the target satisfy the Chant’s actual voice, hearing, perception and line-of-effect requirements. The living ally is at 3/10 normal HP within 15 feet, has no Wounds or other healing modifiers/blockers, and has not received Chant of Renewal healing this round. Mira starts the Chant, pays 2 RP, starts concentration and rolls a 4: **4 + C 3 = 7 healing**, bringing the ally to 10 HP. Starting gains the one eligible Crescendo stack, not a five-stack rider. At 0 RP she cannot pay the next turn’s 1-RP maintenance. Without a genuine intervening recovery, the Chant ends at that turn’s end with no second pulse. The selected feature can offer three pulses; her current resources fund only one. This is no Wound treatment, free Echo or reset of the preceding encounter.

The added healing premise matters: an ally subject to the existing three-Wound Critical healing ceiling cannot simply be assumed to reach 10/10. With that cap, this example would reach **9/10** instead. The correction establishes a clean example; it does not waive the cap.

Replace the **Preventing a hit** paragraph with:

> **Preventing a hit with 2 RP and an available Reaction.** In this separate fixture, Mira is in Mobile stance and has 2 RP, 0 Dissonance, no remembered ordinary spell and an available Reaction, with no condition barring the cast. Before the trigger, her flute is already held in a hand containing no other object; she can provide V and use that hand for S/F. This does not grant a free off-turn draw. When Mira becomes the legal target of an attack, she can commit Shield before that attack resolves. AC becomes 18. An attack total of 15 then misses. RP becomes 0, and a first ordinary rank-1 cast adds 1 Dissonance. Shield expires at her next regular-turn start. Casting it after HP has already been lost would be too late. A previously spent Reaction, an applicable Reaction prohibition, missing components or only 1 RP would prevent activation. Keep the spell’s actual trigger; this example does not introduce an outside game’s casting window.

**Do not change Shield to an imported “must declare before the attack roll” rule.** Its supplied operational record governs the window.

### NWX-05 — Remove the stale active crafting gate

**Affected:** Director Guide **Keep the expedition and records coherent**; `START_HERE.md`, recipe-pass enumeration.  
**Earlier authority: KEEP** the fulfilled advanced promotion and subsequent navigation receipts.

Replace:

> “The remaining advanced recipes and the full expedition/Haven loop retain their review gates.”

with:

> All 687 recipes, including all 433 public recipes, have completed their authored-operational review gates in their stated scopes. Actual ingredient availability, particular-operation prerequisites, runtime and human balance remain separate; the full expedition/Haven integration and final whole-game flow gates are still open. Do not reopen the fulfilled gathering or advanced-recipe review merely because preserved preparation packets call them pending.

`START_HERE` already has the correct totals, but its following enumeration still lists only twelve trades. Replace that enumeration’s first sentence with:

> The completed recipe review covers all 16 trades: Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Cooking, Enchanting, Fishing, Herbalism, Jewelcrafting, Leatherworking, Mining, Poisoncrafting, Rune Carving, Salvaging, Scribing, Skinning, Tailoring and Tinkering.

Preserve the original navigation versions and receipts. This is a current teaching/navigation correction, not a change to historical promotion evidence.

### NWX-06 — Distinguish the expedition charter from the player-promise charter

**Affected:** `DESIGN_CHARTER_CANDIDATE.md`, opening paragraph beginning **“A successful withdrawal…”**  
**Earlier source: KEEP** `GAMEPLAY_LOOP_CANON.md` §4, **Expedition objectives and abort conditions**.

Replace:

> “The charter’s casualty, reserve-supply and return-time limits make those choices concrete.”

with:

> The party’s expedition charter records its casualty, reserve-Supply and latest-return limits. Those expedition-specific thresholds make withdrawal choices concrete; this player-promise charter supplies no new numerical limits or independent withdrawal procedure.

Everything else in the charter is retained within its stated editorial scope. Its priority order follows the locked doctrine; calibration targets are not presented as observed probabilities; actual stage schedules and advancement continuity remain controlling.

This clarification does **not** settle the unresolved expedition/Haven cases or interpret deferred setting material.

## NW-01–20 dispositions

| Case | Verdict | Exact assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **NW-01** | **KEEP** | All six session-zero steps and twelve agreement rows provide meaningful pause/skip, consent, absence, accessibility and privacy procedures without changing fictional permissions. |
| **NW-02** | **KEEP creation; NWX-01** | Creation adds no unauthorized grant. The missing mandatory stance choice is supplied in turn teaching. Linked draft options are not automatically approved. |
| **NW-03** | **KEEP** | Mira’s abilities, HP, RP, proficiency, seven skills, saves, tools and languages match the selected records. |
| **NW-04** | **KEEP values/access; NWX-04** | Four Base actives and four ordinary spells are separate legal selections. Define S/C; no later grant moves to level 1. |
| **NW-05** | **KEEP** | All inventory, coin, Load, Burden and Speed arithmetic is correct. Physical fit remains an actual prerequisite. |
| **NW-06** | **NWX-01/04; otherwise KEEP** | AC, dagger and focus rules are correct. Explicit stance and already-held focus complete the example’s use state. |
| **NW-07** | **KEEP** | Task degrees, attack resolution and binary saves remain separate. No margin-based attack critical is introduced. |
| **NW-08** | **NWX-01; KEEP transitions** | Mobile declarations complete the two-turn state without changing damage, RP, Crescendo, Echo or recharge results. |
| **NW-09** | **KEEP** | Teaching enemy/ally values are not bestiary or balance claims; genuine encounter predicates prevent rehearsal farming. |
| **NW-10** | **NWX-04** | State the clean healing fixture explicitly. No free maintenance, Wound cure, second pulse or Echo follows. |
| **NW-11** | **NWX-04; KEEP spell rule** | Shield requires actual components and permitted Reaction; 2 RP works, 1 RP does not. Preserve its actual before-resolution window. |
| **NW-12** | **KEEP Mira aid; NWX-03** | The example already has adjacency, charge, hand, Action and lawful recovery. Complete the general player summary. |
| **NW-13** | **KEEP sequence; NWX-02** | Dissonance 0/0/1/0/2 is correct. Quiet turns and Retune do not erase repetition history. |
| **NW-14** | **NWX-02; otherwise KEEP** | Retune 4 capped at 2 and advancement 17 HP/3 RP are correct; current damage and spent resources remain. |
| **NW-15** | **NWX-01/02/03; otherwise KEEP** | Start, damage/Wound/death ordering and Oracle RC summaries agree with their governors. Complete stance, history and kit-use teaching. |
| **NW-16** | **NWX-05 plus link condition** | The contained entry path is usable. Correct stale status; distinguish absent optional repository destinations from missing necessary rules. |
| **NW-17** | **KEEP synthesis with NWX-06** | Doctrine and ordinary loop synthesis are faithful. Clarify which charter owns expedition limits; no calibration or unsettled flow approval. |
|
